html:
The largest city in Australia, on the harbour of Port Jackson on the southeast coast. It began in 1788 as a British prison colony and is the capital of New South Wales.

The land around the harbour belongs to the Eora peoples, such as the Gadigal, and their neighbours the Dharug and Tharawal. In January 1788 the First Fleet under Arthur Phillip landed about a thousand people, most of them convicts, at Sydney Cove. A year later smallpox swept through the Aboriginal people of the harbour and killed a large share of them.

The colony survived early hunger and grew on wool, then on the gold rushes of the 1850s, and free settlers came to outnumber convicts. By 1900 Sydney and Melbourne were rivals, so when Australia federated in 1901 a new capital, Canberra, was built between them.

Two landmarks define the city: the Sydney Harbour Bridge, opened in 1932, and the Sydney Opera House, opened in 1973. Sydney held the Olympic Games in 2000. In the Black Summer of 2019 and 2020 smoke from the fires choked the city for weeks.
sum: The largest city in Australia, on the harbour of Port Jackson on the southeast coast. It began in 1788 as a British prison colony and is the capital of New South Wales.
